test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 05 Jul, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

There was a noise that __was wake me up. __
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"wake"** means to stop sleeping; to rouse from sleep. (जागना)

 
 
• **Example: **I usually** wake up** at 6 AM every day.
 
 
 
• **"woke"** is the past tense of "wake," which means it indicates an action that has already happened. (जाग गया)
 
 
• **Example: **She **woke** up early to catch the sunrise.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: has woke me up **(जाग गया है): Incorrect use of tense. "Has woke" should be "has woken."

 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: The alarm has woke me up.
 
• Correct: The alarm has woken me up.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: wakes me up **(जगाता है): Incorrect tense for the context. "Wakes" is present tense.
 
 
• **Example: **The loud noise wakes me up every morning.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: woken me up** (जगाया है): Incorrect without auxiliary verb. Correct form is "has woken me up."
 
 
• **Example:** She has woken me up every day this week.
